audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven level rows were wrong in BOTH layers. The chart gave Tryndamere levels 2, 3 and first item and called levels 1 and 4-5 contested, while the packet chart reads Olaf/Olaf/Olaf/Olaf/Skill/Skill/Tryndamere and the prose says 'Levels 1-3 are yours' and 'This is your strongest stretch'.
audit.why: The page told a reader who has just been shown 'levels 1-3 are yours' that he loses levels 2 and 3.
audit.corrected: All five rows proposed as one group, phases[N].side and win[N] in matched pairs, ratings moved to follow, and five phase whys rewritten. Level 6 (Skill) and 2+ items (Tryndamere) were already right.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page said 'his spin heals off fury', that Ragnarok 'strips his W-slow' and makes you 'unstoppable into him', and gave Undying Rage a '5-second 1-HP window'.
audit.why: The heal is Bloodlust (Q, 12s), which consumes Fury — Spinning Slash heals nothing, so a player kiting 'his spin heal' is watching the wrong bar. And Mocking Shout's slow applies ONLY to enemies with their backs turned to him: face Tryndamere and walk at him and the slow never lands, which is a far better answer than an ultimate. Riot's Undying Rage text gives no duration, so the 5-second figure is unsourced. Ragnarok also does nothing about his immortality — it covers disables.
audit.corrected: Moved the heal to Bloodlust, wrote in the backs-turned condition on Mocking Shout in three places, removed the invented 5-second figure, and stopped Ragnarok being credited with answers it does not have.

audit.why: Undying Rage is 120s at rank 1 and Bloodlust 12s — concrete numbers turn 'respect his ultimate' into a plan.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Undying Rage's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.

edits.after: Bloodlust is the heal and it spends his Fury bar — Executioner's Calling early makes every one of his resets much worse.

edits.before: Tryndamere wastes Undying Rage — commit the full pattern immediately.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are yours. Your Q axe slows him so he can't spin-kite away, and once you have E you land a guaranteed true-damage chunk his pre-fury autos can't match. Open trades with Q to stick the slow, then walk in for E and let your passive ramp attack speed as you take a little spin damage back. Don't chase him through his W-slow + dropback without your axe down to pick back up, and respect that his spin heals off fury — short, decisive trades beat him, drawn-out ones feed his sustain.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours. Your Q axe slows him so he can't spin away, and once you have E you land a guaranteed true-damage chunk his pre-Fury autos can't match. Open trades with Q to stick the slow, then walk in for E and let your passive ramp attack speed as you take a little damage back. Mocking Shout only slows enemies whose backs are turned, so never retreat through it — face him. And the heal is Bloodlust (12s), which spends his Fury: short decisive trades beat him, drawn-out ones pay for it.

edits.before: This is your strongest stretch — keep forcing short all-ins. Chain Q throws to perma-slow him, W for omnivamp, and E true damage straight through his health bar; his crit isn't online yet so you out-trade and out-sustain. At 6 your Ragnarok ignores his W-slow and makes you unstoppable into him, but be honest about R Undying Rage: even a perfectly won trade often ends with him surviving at 1 HP and spinning away. Burn his R if you must, then look to dive with your jungler before it's back up — a wasted Undying Rage is a free kill window later.
edits.after: This is your strongest stretch — keep forcing short all-ins. Chain Q throws to perma-slow him, W for the shield, and E true damage straight through his health bar; his crit isn't online yet so you out-trade and out-sustain. At 6 be honest about Undying Rage: even a perfectly won trade often ends with him surviving on a sliver and spinning away, and Ragnarok does nothing about that — it covers disables, not his immortality. Burn the ultimate if you must, then dive with your jungler before its 120s is back.

edits.before: This window flips to him. Once Trynd stacks Infinity Edge and crit, his spin out-DPSes your flat true damage and his W-slow plus dropback let him kite you while Undying Rage erases your all-in. Your job was to make the game end before this — convert your level 1-to-6 lead into towers, dives and objectives so his scaling never gets to matter. In a straight late-game 1v1 he wins; don't isolate yourself splitpushing into a fed Trynd, group and let your team's CC lock down what your Ragnarok can't finish.
edits.after: This window flips to him. Once Trynd stacks Infinity Edge and crit, Spinning Slash out-DPSes your flat true damage and Undying Rage erases your all-in outright. Your job was to make the game end before this — convert your level 1-to-6 lead into towers, dives and objectives so his scaling never gets to matter. In a straight late-game 1v1 he wins; don't isolate yourself splitpushing into a fed Trynd. Group, and let your team's CC land in the window right after his ultimate ends.

notes: The packet's suspectName hit on 'Undying Rage's' in wants.foe[1] is a FALSE POSITIVE — the name is correct, the possessive apostrophe produced the edit distance. What was actually wrong in that string was the unsourced '5-second 1-HP window'; Riot's text gives no duration, so the number is gone rather than restated. The single highest-value addition here is Mocking Shout's backs-turned condition, which appeared nowhere on the page and changes how the player walks in every trade.
